[LGRA.2.9.6.9] An unescaped `{` in an interpolation-eligible string
([LGRA.2.9.6.8]) whose brace span has a body that is not a valid
`interp_body` ([LGRA.2.9.6.1]) — a body containing an operator or any
token outside the `NAME ( '.' NAME | '[' INT_LIT ']' )*` path
grammar, e.g. `{c.a + c.b}` — is a compile error
(`DS_VALIDATE_INTERP_BAD_PATH`). The compiler must not emit such a span
as literal text. A computed value in an interpolation is expressed by
binding it with a `let` and interpolating the bound name.

A **valid** `interp_body` is refused with `DS_VALIDATE_INTERP_UNSUPPORTED`, and
likewise never emitted as literal text, in two cases. In the first, its value
kind is one a compiler cannot render: the code is distinct from
`DS_VALIDATE_INTERP_BAD_PATH` for the reason [LCST.4.5.3] gives for its cast pair,
that the program is well-formed and the compiler is incomplete. In the second, it
is a whole `Json` value, which is not a leaf ([LGRA.2.9.6.11]): the program
breaks a rule, and the compiler must refuse it however complete it is.
